Other related examples report 56% in 30 h under NaH/DMF and 50% in 30 h with DMF listed but no separate base. A related, but distinct, trichloropyrimidine example reports NaH/DMF and 71.7% yield after 5 h.

These precedents support displacement of the activated heteroaryl chloride by the partner’s **alcohol-derived oxygen** to form an ether. They do **not** support an amino-driven addition-annulation; the partner shown contains a hydroxymethyl group, not an amino group. Exact conditions and yield for the queried substrate remain unverified.

The product is consistent with replacement of the activated heteroaryl chloride by the partner’s alcohol oxygen, giving an O-linked ether; the closest reaction records favor NaH/DMF, while the exact pair was not found. The product is consistent with **displacement of the activated heteroaryl chloride by the alcohol-derived oxygen** (an O-substitution/SNAr-type reaction).

**Best-supported conditions:** sodium hydride (**NaH**) as base in **DMF**. Close reaction analogues report this combination, though the exact substrate pair was not located. **DMF is the solvent**, while NaH would generate the alkoxide nucleophile.

Other bases such as **K₂CO₃** or **Cs₂CO₃** could be considered as alternatives, but they are general suggestions—not conditions confirmed by the matching records.
